item.title: Komyshuvakha toll rises to 40 as Brussels talks on Ukraine's security guarantees open
item.description:
The death toll from Russia's bombing of an aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 40 on Wednesday, Reuters reports, with dozens still missing as search-and-rescue work entered its third day. Regional official Ivan Fedorov put the missing at 59, while President Volodymyr Zelensky said more than 30 people may still be trapped under the rubble. Two rescue workers and four police officers are among the dead, according to Ukraine's emergency services. The Institute for the Study of War, in its November 4 assessment, likewise puts the toll at at least 40 and notes the strike hit a humanitarian aid station southeast of Zaporizhzhia city.
Zelensky's account, repeated in the Reuters reporting, is that Russian forces first dropped aerial bombs on an underground school building being used as a distribution point as people arrived to collect aid, then struck the shelter with more bombs — a "double-tap" pattern, as the Kyiv Independent's coverage, carried by EuropeSays, describes it, with nine guided aerial bombs reported. Reuters also reports verified bodycam footage from one of the policemen killed, showing residents rushing into an underground shelter moments before a large explosion. Russia's defence ministry, by contrast, maintains the attack targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, killing up to 25 servicemen — a claim that does not explain the reported civilian toll at an aid site and has not been independently verified. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians.
For ordinary people in the village, the practical consequences are immediate and grim: the regional administration said the Zaporizhzhia budget will cover funeral costs, with moderate-injury victims receiving about Hr.20,000 (about $440) and severe-injury victims up to about Hr.50,000 (about $1,100), according to EuropeSays. More broadly, the strike landed a day after a brief US-brokered local ceasefire for evacuations from occupied Oleshky expired, and less than a week before US envoy Steve Witkoff's Abu Dhabi talks on November 10–11, which are to cover post-war security agreements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures. On Wednesday, officials from Ukraine, the United States, Germany, France, Britain, NATO and the European Union met at the European Commission's headquarters in Brussels on security guarantees, reconstruction and post-war economic opportunities — the meeting already flagged in the morning brief, with a separate NATO security-guarantee session due Thursday. No outcome from Wednesday's Brussels session had been reported in the coverage checked by brief time.
In short: 40 dead in Komyshuvakha, 59 missing by one official count, more than 30 possibly still under rubble, Russia still claiming a military target — and in Brussels, the allies spent Wednesday trying to turn security-guarantee talk into something Kyiv can take to Abu Dhabi.
Sources:
Source: mymixfm.com.

Russia's defence ministry, by contrast, maintains the attack targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, killing up to 25 servicemen — a claim that does not explain the reported civilian toll at an aid site and has not been independently verified. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians.

For ordinary people in the village, the practical consequences are immediate and grim: the regional administration said the Zaporizhzhia budget will cover funeral costs, with moderate-injury victims receiving about Hr.20,000 (about $440) and severe-injury victims up to about Hr.50,000 (about $1,100), according to EuropeSays. More broadly, the strike landed a day after a brief US-brokered local ceasefire for evacuations from occupied Oleshky expired, and less than a week before US envoy Steve Witkoff's Abu Dhabi talks on November 10–11, which are to cover post-war security agreements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures. On Wednesday, officials from Ukraine, the United States, Germany, France, Britain, NATO and the European Union met at the European Commission's headquarters in Brussels on security guarantees, reconstruction and post-war economic opportunities — the meeting already flagged in the morning brief, with a separate NATO security-guarantee session due Thursday. No outcome from Wednesday's Brussels session had been reported in the coverage checked by brief time.

In short: 40 dead in Komyshuvakha, 59 missing by one official count, more than 30 possibly still under rubble, Russia still claiming a military target — and in Brussels, the allies spent Wednesday trying to turn security-guarantee talk into something Kyiv can take to Abu Dhabi.

Sources:

Source: mymixfm.com — Read the full article

item.title: Houthis claim a new round of Saudi strikes as Turkey's pact vote looms — and Riyadh stays silent on the airport claim
item.description:
Yemen's Houthis claimed a fresh series of strikes against Saudi targets on Wednesday, according to Demócrata's account of spokesman Yahya Saree's statements: a ballistic missile that "directly" hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, causing what Saree called significant damage, plus a drone strike on a radar installation on the Al Qahma peninsula, a ballistic missile on a camp in Najran, a strike on a Border Guard command-and-control building in Jizan, six ballistic missiles on Saudi reinforcements east of Al Jawf governorate, and a downed reconnaissance drone over Taiz. Saree again urged airlines, workers and passengers to avoid Saudi airspace, except over Mecca and Medina. Saudi authorities had not provided an official version of the airport claim by the time of that reporting — so the airport hit, like the morning's claim, remains unverified, and should be read as a Houthi claim, not a confirmed strike.
The backdrop has not eased. The US Mission in Saudi Arabia warned American citizens on Monday of potential Houthi attacks, airspace closures and flight disruptions, the Philippine News Agency reports, noting the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted two drones over the Riyadh region on Monday, and that civil-defence alerts for Khamis Mushait, Abha, Taif and Najran were later lifted. A separate Dubai Standard roundup notes Hormuz traffic has collapsed — only five commodity-carrying ships passed through on Saturday, none on Sunday, against more than 130 a day before the conflict — and Brent crude was trading around $103 a barrel on Wednesday morning. Meanwhile Turkey's parliament was set on Wednesday to ratify the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, Reuters reported in the morning, with a collective-defence clause mirroring NATO's Article 5; ratification alone would not send Turkish troops, which need a separate mandate. No confirmed vote result had appeared in English-language coverage checked by 5 PM CT, so this brief does not claim the pact passed — watch the night brief for the result.
For ordinary people, the through-line is travel and fuel: Riyadh airport claims, confirmed or not, keep airlines and passengers guessing, US staff face tighter travel rules, and Gulf shipping remains a fraction of normal, which is exactly the pressure Iran and the Houthis are applying while Tehran says Washington's answer to its seven conditions is still "not convincing."
In short: the Houthis claimed a Wednesday missile hit on Riyadh airport plus five other operations, Riyadh has not confirmed the airport claim, US warnings to citizens stand, Hormuz traffic is near-empty — and Turkey's pact ratification was due Wednesday, with its result still unconfirmed at brief time.
Sources:
Source: democrata.es.

item.title: Poland — most Poles back neither side in the tribunal crisis, new polls say:
item.description:
A United Surveys/IBRiS poll for Wirtualna Polska, published Tuesday, found 38.6% of Poles believe neither Prime Minister Donald Tusk's government nor President Karol Nawrocki is right in the Constitutional Tribunal dispute, against 28.7% backing Nawrocki and 26.6% backing Tusk's government; among 18–29-year-olds, 64% sided with neither.
A separate Europion Polska poll for Onet (November 1–2) found 30% supporting the judges behind the tribunal leadership's suspension against 21% backing the existing leadership. Separately, the International Commission of Jurists criticised both the group of judges who suspended the tribunal's president and deputy and Nawrocki's refusal to swear in five parliament-elected judges.
No new Tusk–Nawrocki meeting date was announced Wednesday; the presidential palace has said a meeting could happen within days. Sources:
Source: hungarianconservative.com.

item.title: Apple — Siri AI opens to every developer in the iOS 27.3 beta, but users won't see it for months:
item.description:
Apple announced November 3 that a Developer Preview in the iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3 and visionOS 27.3 betas lets any developer bring an app's content and actions into Siri AI via App Intents, with new "skills" to chain several actions into one experience.
This is a testing surface, not a launch: App Store submissions with Siri AI integrations open in spring 2027, first customer integrations arrive "in a few months," and Siri AI remains unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS and watchOS and for users under 13. Apple is running developer labs November 4–5.
Sources:
Source: eweek.com.

item.title: Google — DeepMind's Antigravity gets cheminformatics skills for drug discovery:
item.description:
Google DeepMind announced November 3 that Google Antigravity, its agentic system, now has Cheminformatics Skills: searching compound databases (ChEMBL, PubChem), matched molecular pair analysis, and proposing novel rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes — in its example workflow, thousands of compounds searched and candidates proposed within an hour.
DeepMind stresses the designs are testable hypotheses, not finished drugs, and still need synthesis and lab validation; up to 10,000 scientists are offered the top usage tier free for six months. Sources:
Source: dnainsider.news.

item.title: flitai-io/gpuworks — ZStack open-sources its GPU management platform:
item.description:
ZStack announced November 4 that GPUWorks is now open source under Apache 2.0: a GPU-server management and model-serving platform with a control plane plus web UI described as a roughly 40 MB download, deploying with one command and no pre-existing Kubernetes cluster required, serving models through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
The vendor claim to scrutinise: one GPUWorks server managed 1,003 GPU servers in a test, bringing up 500+ inference replicas in 4 minutes — no GPU model, per-server GPU count or network layout published, and no independent verification yet. Source:
Source: tech-insider.org.

item.title: Binance — Recovery Update #7: 98% replenished, reserves snapshot now covers 44 tokens:
item.description:
Binance said November 4 it has replenished about 98% of the roughly $6.3B affected by its October security incident, up from 95% on November 2, with the remaining ~2% in less-liquid tokens being bought through market and OTC channels and expected to be slower, with no completion date given.
A new proof-of-reserves snapshot taken at 00:00 UTC November 4 covers 44 tokens, up from 10 in the October 31 snapshot, but the full zero-knowledge proof will take about 50–60 hours to generate — so the wider snapshot is not yet independently verifiable. Binance repeats it covers the losses from its own resources, not users'.
These are company statements, not an independent audit. Sources:
Source: binance.com.

item.title: CISA KEV, November 4 — old Apple WebKit flaw added as APT29 campaign targets unpatched phones:
item.description:
CISA added Apple CVE-2024-27834 (WebKit pointer-authentication bypass, fixed May 2024, CVSS 5.5) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 4, catalog version 2026.11.04 with 1,768 entries, federal deadline November 18.
The timing lines up with Sekoia's "Poisoned Source" research tying Russia-linked APT29 to attacks on iOS and Android users via hacked websites, lookalike sites and a tampered analytics script, using older exploit chains against phones that missed updates. If your iPhone is on a current OS, this flaw is already patched — the risk is unpatched devices.
Sources:
Source: carthageelectronics.com.

item.title: Zyxel GS1900 zero-day — the switch takeover blamed on the wrong bug:
item.description:
GreyNoise's September report of 996 Zyxel GS1900 switches taken over in 48 countries (configuration files and hashed root passwords pulled) was blamed at the time on CVE-2026-7273, fixed in June — but researchers now say the attackers actually used a new zero-day, CVE-2026-107441 (CVSS 8.8), fixed in Zyxel's October 22 firmware.
Lock down switch management interfaces and update to that firmware. Source:
Source: carthageelectronics.com.

item.title: Israel's consultations, day one: Eisenkot ahead on expected recommendations, but neither man has 61 — and the Arab parties and UTJ hold the balance
item.description:
President Isaac Herzog opened consultations with the factions of the 26th Knesset on Wednesday evening, hearing the smallest parties first in a break from custom — Religious Zionism-Zehut first at 5 PM, then Shas and Yisrael Beiteinu — with the larger parties, including Yashar and Likud, due Thursday evening, JFeed reports. Herzog told the factions beforehand that he holds "very broad discretion" over who gets the first mandate, and that no party clearly won and not every campaign promise can be kept. The certified count, already covered in the morning brief, stands at 53 for Netanyahu's bloc, 48 for Eisenkot's, and a record 19 for the Arab-led parties, with 61 needed.
Wednesday's new information is the recommendation arithmetic. Ynet's tally, reported by JFeed, gives Eisenkot 48 expected recommendations — from Yashar, B'Yachad, the Democrats and Yisrael Beiteinu — against 46 for Netanyahu, from Likud, Otzma Yehudit, Shas and Religious Zionism. The Joint List, Ra'am and United Torah Judaism have not committed. The Jewish Weekly, meanwhile, reports both major Arab lists, Ra'am and the Joint List, have announced they will recommend Eisenkot — which would take him to 67 recommendations — while warning that recommending a candidate does not commit a party to supporting the government he then proposes, that Ra'am's position on an Eisenkot administration remains uncertain, and that Joint List support for a government is considered extremely unlikely. UTJ, with seven seats, is the other unresolved piece: it has yet to announce its recommendation. Herzog has not ruled out a second round of consultations, and the mandate is likely to be handed out sometime from Friday through next Tuesday; the nominee then gets 28 days, extendable by 14.
The two camps' arguments are mirror images. Netanyahu's camp, which had accused Arab groupings of having "stolen" the vote, saw that claim undercut Wednesday when the Central Elections Committee said its review found no irregularities compromising the election or changing its results. Eisenkot's camp argues the opposition's combined strength — parties opposed to Netanyahu hold 67 seats against his bloc's 53 — entitles him to the first attempt, and is already eyeing replacing the Knesset speaker, with Yair Lapid viewed as a likely candidate. For ordinary Israelis, nothing changes yet: Netanyahu remains in office, the new Knesset is sworn in November 10 regardless, and the paths — an Eisenkot government with Arab support, a unity arrangement, or failure and new elections — are all still open.
In short: day one of consultations leaves Eisenkot ahead on paper (48, or 67 with both Arab lists), Netanyahu at 46, UTJ uncommitted — and Herzog, who says the choice is his discretion, not an automatic tally, likely decides between Friday and next Tuesday.
Sources:
Source: jfeed.com.

item.title: Russell Brand — second day of deliberations ends with no verdict, jury resumes Thursday:
item.description:
Brand returned to Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday with his wife Laura Gallacher for the second day of jury deliberations.
The jury of eight men and four women, which began deliberating Tuesday just before 14:50 GMT, ended Wednesday without a verdict; Judge Joel Bennathan told jurors to stop deliberating for the day, and the trial resumes November 5. Brand, 51, denies three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault, involving six women over 1999–2009, and only unanimous verdicts will be accepted.
Nothing here is a finding of guilt. Sources:
Source: oxygen.com.

item.title: Overnight drone war hits Ukraine's grid again, Komyshuvakha toll rises to 37, and Brussels talks open today
item.description:
Russia launched 310 drones at Ukraine overnight into Wednesday, November 4, according to Ukraine's air force, which said it downed or suppressed 272 of them, with hits recorded at 19 locations and debris falling at 15 others. Regional officials reported energy facilities struck in at least six regions — Ternopil, Kirovohrad, Rivne, Volyn, Odesa and Zhytomyr — and President Volodymyr Zelensky said damage stretched across nine regions in all, including power generation facilities and substations, with emergency and unscheduled outages continuing in many cities and communities. In Odesa, a shopping centre and residential homes were hit, though no one was injured there, according to regional head Oleh Kiper; in Rivne, a residential building was partially destroyed and a woman was injured; in Volyn, a large part of the region lost power before settlements were reconnected by morning. Kyiv and surrounding regions reported power and water outages, and an industrial facility in Dnipro was hit, injuring two men.
The other side's account of the night looks very different, as usual. Russia's defence ministry said it shot down 709 Ukrainian drones overnight over 14 Russian regions, occupied Crimea and the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea — a figure Ukraine has not confirmed and that cannot be independently checked. What is confirmed from the Russian side is that Ukrainian drones hit a large Ozon logistics complex in Adygeysk, southern Russia, setting it on fire and forcing evacuations, with no injuries reported, according to the head of the Republic of Adygea, Murat Kumpilov. Russian officials also said eight people, including four children, were injured when Ukrainian strikes hit apartment buildings and cars on the border, and that a cargo ship carrying supplies for Ukraine's military was hit in the Black Sea. Russia's ministry said its own strikes hit power substations in the Kyiv and Zhytomyr regions, framing the campaign as continued targeting of energy infrastructure.
The human toll from Monday's strike is still rising, and that is the grimmest number in this brief. Reuters reported Wednesday that the death toll from the bombing of the aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, has risen to 37, with dozens still missing — regional official Ivan Fedorov put the missing at 59 — as rescuers continue searching the rubble of the former school. Zelensky says Russian forces first dropped aerial bombs on the school as people arrived to collect aid, then struck the shelter with more bombs. Russia's defence ministry, by contrast, maintains the attack targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, killing up to 25 servicemen — a claim the BBC previously reported it found no credible evidence for. Treat the 37 figure as the latest official count, not a final one, while the rubble is still being cleared.
For ordinary Ukrainians, the practical meaning is another winter morning of outages: the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry has accused Russia of crimes against humanity over its energy strikes, saying they are deliberate and part of a state policy of depriving civilians of essential energy — a charge Moscow rejects in its framing of the strikes as military targeting. The diplomatic clock, meanwhile, is ticking in Brussels today. The European Commission is hosting representatives from Ukraine, the United States, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, NATO and the World Bank to discuss a "prosperity plan" and security guarantees for Ukraine, building on earlier talks in Miami, with a separate NATO session on security guarantees due Thursday. Zelensky has said he wants US guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5 and backed by a congressional vote, and has rejected a repeat of the 1994 Budapest Memorandum assurances. All of this leads to the US-brokered trilateral talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11, which Moscow has confirmed it will attend, with Kyiv seeking an end to energy strikes and a Black Sea ceasefire among its priorities.
In short: 310 Russian drones overnight, 272 claimed downed, power and water hit across Ukraine, the Komyshuvakha toll now 37 with dozens missing, Ukrainian drones burning an Ozon warehouse inside Russia — and today in Brussels, the allies try to agree what security guarantees are actually on offer before Abu Dhabi.
Sources:
Source: q106fm.com.

Reuters reported Wednesday that the death toll from the bombing of the aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, has risen to 37, with dozens still missing — regional official Ivan Fedorov put the missing at 59 — as rescuers continue searching the rubble of the former school. Zelensky says Russian forces first dropped aerial bombs on the school as people arrived to collect aid, then struck the shelter with more bombs. Russia's defence ministry, by contrast, maintains the attack targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, killing up to 25 servicemen — a claim the BBC previously reported it found no credible evidence for. Treat the 37 figure as the latest official count, not a final one, while the rubble is still being cleared.

For ordinary Ukrainians, the practical meaning is another winter morning of outages: the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry has accused Russia of crimes against humanity over its energy strikes, saying they are deliberate and part of a state policy of depriving civilians of essential energy — a charge Moscow rejects in its framing of the strikes as military targeting. The diplomatic clock, meanwhile, is ticking in Brussels today. The European Commission is hosting representatives from Ukraine, the United States, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, NATO and the World Bank to discuss a "prosperity plan" and security guarantees for Ukraine, building on earlier talks in Miami, with a separate NATO session on security guarantees due Thursday. Zelensky has said he wants US guarantees modelled on NATO's Article 5 and backed by a congressional vote, and has rejected a repeat of the 1994 Budapest Memorandum assurances. All of this leads to the US-brokered trilateral talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11, which Moscow has confirmed it will attend, with Kyiv seeking an end to energy strikes and a Black Sea ceasefire among its priorities.

In short: 310 Russian drones overnight, 272 claimed downed, power and water hit across Ukraine, the Komyshuvakha toll now 37 with dozens missing, Ukrainian drones burning an Ozon warehouse inside Russia — and today in Brussels, the allies try to agree what security guarantees are actually on offer before Abu Dhabi.

Source: q106fm.com — Read the full article

item.title: Turkey set to ratify a Saudi defence pact as Houthis claim a Riyadh airport strike and Iran says a deal is still far off
item.description:
Turkey's parliament was set on Wednesday to ratify a defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan that includes a collective-defence clause, Reuters reports — committing NATO's second-largest army to Riyadh's defence as the kingdom faces attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed by the three countries in August, mirrors NATO's Article 5 in treating an attack on one member as an attack on all, and plans deeper defence-industry cooperation and military coordination. Ratification alone does not send Turkish forces to Saudi Arabia: deploying personnel would need a separate parliamentary mandate, which a ruling-party lawmaker told Reuters Turkey would also submit. Defence Minister Yasar Guler has said he did not see Turkish troops engaging in combat or offensive operations against the Houthis, and officials told Reuters last month that Turkey's contribution was expected to be limited to equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems — though analysts told Reuters that Turkish troops and advisers could later deploy to install and operate systems sent by Ankara once a deployment mandate passes.
The pact's timing matters because the Houthi campaign has not paused. On Wednesday the Houthis said they had targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Reuters reports via Devdiscourse, with no confirmation from Saudi authorities, and the group again urged international airlines to refrain from flying over Saudi airspace. That claim sits in the same unverified category as Tuesday's rival claims — the coalition's claimed drone interception over the Mecca region, which the Houthis called a "slanderous and recycled lie," and their claimed strikes on Abha airport and Khamis Mushait air base — and it should be read that way until Riyadh confirms or denies it. What is firmer is the diplomatic backdrop: a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Tehran and Washington remain "far from a deal" to end their war, and Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the US response to Iran's seven conditions — including waiving oil sanctions, ending the naval blockade and releasing frozen funds — was "not convincing," adding that the Strait of Hormuz would only reopen if Washington fully and explicitly met them. President Donald Trump, in a Fox News interview on Tuesday, said he was ready and "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," and declined to rule out a resumption of US combat operations after the US elections.
For ordinary people in the region, the stakes are flights, fuel and shipping: Riyadh airport has partially reopened after earlier closures, Jeddah and Dammam still face delays and cancellations, and the US Mission has tightened its own travel rules for staff. A ratified pact does not end the Houthi threat, and it does not put Turkish troops on Saudi soil tomorrow — but it does give Riyadh a formal mutual-defence commitment from a major military power, which is exactly the kind of deterrent signal the pact's authors say they intend, and exactly the kind of escalation Tehran and the Houthis will read as a hardening of the Saudi position.
In short: Turkey ratifies a collective-defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan — formal obligation, no troops without a second vote — while the Houthis claim a new Riyadh airport strike Riyadh has not confirmed, and Iran says the US answer on Hormuz is still not good enough.
Sources:
Source: reuters.com.

item.title: Poland: Nawrocki now open to meeting Tusk, government preparing a list of laws for the disputed court
item.description:
President Karol Nawrocki is open to meeting Prime Minister Donald Tusk to discuss the Constitutional Tribunal crisis, his spokesman Rafal Leskiewicz told Polish Radio on Wednesday, though no date has been agreed — following Tusk's offer Tuesday of a private meeting this week.
Separately, the head of the prime minister's chancellery, Jan Grabiec, said Wednesday the government is preparing a list of laws unconsidered by the tribunal for almost 11 years to refer to it, and that the Tusk–Nawrocki meeting would happen "in a matter of the coming days" in a quiet atmosphere. Tusk also accused Russia on Tuesday of trying to exploit the tribunal dispute to fuel instability in Poland.
Sources:
Source: europesays.com.

item.title: floci-io/floci — a free local AWS emulator, the most broadly useful newcomer on GitHub trending Wednesday:
item.description:
Floci is a free, MIT-licensed local emulator of Amazon Web Services, written in Java and compiled to a native binary, for development, testing and CI without a cloud account, authentication tokens or paid features.
It is aimed squarely at former LocalStack Community users, after that free edition was sunset in March 2026 with auth tokens required and security updates frozen. GitDiscover lists it at about 28.8K stars, up 482 on Wednesday.

item.title: Binance — broader reserves snapshot due today, proof still 40–50 hours away:
item.description:
Binance plans a broader-token reserves snapshot on November 4, after completing the zero-knowledge proof for its October 31 snapshot (10 tokens verifiable 1:1) on November 2.
Generating the updated proof is estimated to take about 40–50 hours, so the new snapshot itself is not yet independently verifiable. Binance says it has covered about 95% of the roughly $6.3B stolen on October 29, though a November 3 incident report cited 98% replenished as of October 31 — a discrepancy worth watching, since the two figures are not the same claim.

item.title: Israel's government formation formally opens: Herzog receives certified results, says no party clearly won, and starts with the smallest parties
item.description:
President Isaac Herzog received the certified results of Israel's October 27 election on Wednesday, November 4, and opened the consultations that will decide who gets the first mandate to form a government — and, in his opening remarks, said no party clearly won and urged leaders to accept that not every campaign promise can be kept. The count, certified by Central Elections Committee chair Justice Noam Sohlberg, gives Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc 48, and the Arab-led parties a record 19, in a 120-seat Knesset where 61 are needed for a majority. No candidate had been given the mandate by Wednesday evening Israel time, and Herzog has seven days from the formal announcement to assign it; the nominee then gets 28 days, extendable by 14, to form a government.
The two camps' positions are already staked out, and they do not add up to 61 on their own. Netanyahu's allies Religious Zionism and Shas have said they will recommend Netanyahu, while the five opposition leaders who met in Herzliya on Tuesday agreed all their parties will recommend Eisenkot. The Arab-led parties' 19 seats are the arithmetic key — and the political problem: a Joint List source told Fox News Digital the alliance was likely to recommend Eisenkot, while Yisrael Beiteinu leader Avigdor Liberman opposes a government dependent on Arab parties, and Netanyahu has called for a broad coalition without Arab lists after accusing Arab groupings of having "stolen" the vote. That fraud claim took a hit Wednesday: the Central Elections Committee said its review found no evidence of irregularities that compromised the election's integrity or changed its results, undercutting the allegation, according to an Associated Press report carried Wednesday. Eisenkot has said Netanyahu's camp makes the claim "because they lost."
Herzog is hearing factions in ascending order of size, a departure from custom — Religious Zionism first on Wednesday evening, followed by Shas and Yisrael Beiteinu, with the two largest parties, Likud and Eisenkot's Yashar, last on Thursday evening — and his office has not excluded a further round. For ordinary Israelis, the practical effect is continuity with uncertainty: Netanyahu remains in office while talks go on, the new Knesset is sworn in November 10, and the possible paths — an Eisenkot government with Arab support, a Netanyahu–Eisenkot unity arrangement, or failure and new elections — are all still open, with none yet chosen.
In short: certified results confirm 53–48–19 with no majority, the election committee rejects the fraud claim, Herzog opens consultations smallest-first, and the mandate decision — most likely Netanyahu or Eisenkot — is due within seven days.
Sources:
Source: crisis.zone.

item.title: Komyshuvakha toll still disputed, daytime drones continue, and a nuclear-plant employee is reported killed
item.description:
The confirmed death toll from Monday's strike on the humanitarian aid centre in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, still has not settled into a single figure on Tuesday evening — and that disagreement itself is the story. The evening brief put it at 31 dead with more than 45 missing, citing the regional administration. The BBC's later reporting, relayed Tuesday evening, put the confirmed toll at 33, with President Volodymyr Zelensky warning that more than 50 people could still be trapped under the rubble. An earlier BBC/TBS account from Tuesday morning had it at 26, including two emergency rescuers and four police officers, with 27 then reported missing. Rescue work has repeatedly been interrupted by the threat of further Russian drone attacks, according to the regional head, Mykhailo Semikin. Treat any single number tonight as provisional: the counts are moving as rubble is cleared, not because the facts are settled.
The two sides' accounts of what was hit have not moved closer. Zelensky says residents had gathered at a school building used weekly to distribute humanitarian aid, that Russian forces struck the school and then struck again where people had taken shelter, and that "the Russians could not have been unaware" civilians gathered there weekly. Russia's defence ministry, by contrast, said the attack targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen — a claim the BBC reported it found no credible evidence for, noting no major military or industrial facilities in the settlement. The same wave also hit a hospice in Dnipro and a hospital in Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly patients.
The fighting did not stop during the day. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched another 81 drones during Tuesday daytime, including 74 jet-powered models, of which defenders shot down or suppressed 62 — figures separate from the overnight barrage of 289 drones and 76 missiles covered in the earlier briefs. Separately, Reuters reported Tuesday that the management of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant said a Ukrainian drone killed two people in a car, including a female station employee — the third plant employee killed in the past two weeks and the 13th since April, according to the plant. Ukraine did not comment. The plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, is offline, and the UN nuclear watchdog's director general, Rafael Grossi, has repeatedly called for military restraint around it. The plant's statement gave no indication of where the incident occurred, so the location — and whether it was near the plant itself — is unconfirmed.
For ordinary Ukrainians, the practical picture heading into Wednesday is unchanged from the evening brief and still grim: emergency outages in seven regions, Kyiv water cuts, and three DTEK thermal plants halted. Diplomatically, the next marker is Wednesday, November 4, when Zelensky said teams from Ukraine, the US, Europe and NATO countries meet in Brussels to discuss recovery packages and security guarantees, ahead of the US-brokered Abu Dhabi talks on November 10–11 that Moscow has confirmed it will attend.
In short: the Komyshuvakha toll is still disputed — 31, 33, or higher once the rubble is cleared — daytime drone attacks continued, a Zaporizhzhia plant employee is reported killed in a drone strike Ukraine has not commented on, and the next diplomatic step is Wednesday's Brussels meeting, not yet a ceasefire.
Sources:
Source: augerton.com.

item.title: Saudi–Houthi: a disputed drone over Mecca, rival claims over the south-west, and a fresh US travel warning
item.description:
Tuesday's Saudi–Houthi exchange is a case study in two competing versions of the same day, with no independent confirmation of either side's full account. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a drone over the Mecca region on Tuesday, with coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki quoted by the Saudi Press Agency at 12:36 PM local time, and later said two more drones were destroyed — one over the Eastern Province, one heading south — bringing Tuesday's claimed total to three, according to Xinhua's relay. The Houthis rejected the Mecca claim outright: military spokesman Yahya Saree called it a "slanderous and recycled lie," AFP reported, and the movement has systematically denied targeting Islam's holy sites, a point it has made repeatedly in response to earlier Saudi claims about Mecca and Medina.
At the same time, the Houthis made their own claims that could not be independently verified: Saree said the group targeted Abha International Airport with a drone and King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait with a ballistic missile, both in the south-western Asir region. And in the other direction, the Houthis said Saudi-led airstrikes killed 17 civilians over two days, most of them children, hitting residential areas and markets — a claim from Houthi-controlled health authorities that Saudi Arabia has not addressed in the reporting seen. Saree also said Riyadh carried out 109 strikes over the past 24 hours across Saada, Taiz, Lahj, Al-Jawf and Hodeidah. None of these casualty or strike counts is independently verified.
What is on the record from a third party is the US warning. The US Mission to Saudi Arabia updated its security alert on November 3, warning that Houthi attacks have hit civilian airports and critical infrastructure, causing casualties and severe travel disruption, and that hostilities could escalate rapidly beyond the immediate area. US government personnel now need special authorisation to travel to Qatif, Yanbu, Jizan, Asir, Najran and Taif, and may not go within 20 miles of the Yemen border. The alert itself describes no new strike — it is a warning, not a report of one — and it notes Riyadh airport has partially reopened while Jeddah and Dammam face delays and cancellations. That sits alongside the evening brief's report of Houthi ground raids across the south-western border and the Asian Cup postponement to late 2027: the pattern is a war widening from missiles and drones into border raids, event cancellations, and travel restrictions, even on days when the two sides cannot agree on what actually happened.
In short: the coalition claims three drone interceptions including one over Mecca, the Houthis deny the Mecca claim and claim their own strikes in the south-west while reporting 17 civilian deaths from Saudi strikes — none of it independently verified — and the US has tightened its own travel rules for the oil heartland and the Yemen border region.
Sources:
Source: lifenewsagency.com.

item.title: Iran: no new confirmed strike Tuesday evening; the Qeshm account stands as reported, not on the record
item.description:
The limited US strikes on Qeshm Island reported Monday by the Wall Street Journal — described by US officials to the Journal, AP and CNN as defensive strikes after Iranian surface-to-air fire at a US jet and an Iranian missile aimed at commercial shipping — still have no formal CENTCOM statement and no formal Iranian confirmation of a US attack, as of Tuesday evening.
Iran's position, reported Tuesday, remains that a deal is "far off" and Tehran will not accept "excessive demands," while Qatari mediators were due in Tehran on Tuesday night. Oil gave back part of Monday's sharp fall on Tuesday after the strike news broke.
Nothing Tuesday evening changes that picture; treat any new strike claim without an official statement as unverified. Sources:
Source: themedialine.org.

item.title: Poland: no new court move Tuesday evening, but Tusk offers private talks with Nawrocki
item.description:
Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Tuesday, after a National Security Council meeting, that he had offered to meet President Karol Nawrocki privately this week to ease tensions over the Constitutional Tribunal, keeping the timing private so they could speak candidly.
Nawrocki opened the council meeting by calling the suspensions of the tribunal's president and deputy unlawful and blaming Tusk for the police presence outside the court; Tusk called those remarks unnecessarily confrontational. The council also showed broad agreement on expanding the US military presence in Poland and establishing American bases, Tusk said.
This does not resolve Tuesday's split assembly — eight judges meeting and claiming a quorum, seven staying away — covered in the evening brief. Source:
Source: polandinsight.com.

item.title: Chainstack breach disclosed November 3 — customer data and password hashes accessed:
item.description:
Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack said an attacker entered a development environment through a third-party component on October 26, reached production on October 29, was detected and cut off on October 31, and the incident closed November 2.
The attacker accessed a database with organisation names, account-holder names, member email addresses and password hashes, and had access to systems holding node credentials — which Chainstack says it has no evidence were read but is treating as exposed. Customers are being asked to rotate node credentials and regenerate API keys.
The company says services kept running normally and it does not store full payment-card details. Source:
Source: abijita.com.

item.title: Russell Brand — no verdict Tuesday; jury sent home at 4 PM, back Wednesday:
item.description:
The jury at Southwark Crown Court began deliberating Tuesday just before 14:50 GMT after Judge Joel Bennathan finished summing up, and was sent home at 4 PM local time with no verdict, Reuters reports.
Deliberations resume Wednesday morning. Brand denies three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault, involving six women over 1999–2009.
Nothing here is a finding of guilt. Separately, a New York judge on November 3 cleared a civil suit — an anonymous extra's sexual-assault claim against Brand and Warner Bros. from the 2010 shoot of *Arthur* — to proceed toward trial, denying the corporate defendants' motion to dismiss.
That civil ruling is not a verdict either. Sources:
Source: reuters.com.

item.title: Israel — opposition formally lines up behind Eisenkot, Shas behind Netanyahu; Herzog decides from Wednesday:
item.description:
Five opposition leaders met in Herzliya on Tuesday — Eisenkot, former prime minister Naftali Bennett, Avigdor Liberman, Yair Golan and Yair Lapid — and agreed all their parties will recommend Gadi Eisenkot to President Isaac Herzog, with negotiating teams drafting policy guidelines and coalition agreements immediately, according to The Media Line and Crisis.Zone.
The opposition holds 48 seats, Netanyahu's bloc 53, the Arab-led parties 19, with 61 needed — and the leaders have not settled whether to rely on Arab parties, which Liberman opposes. Shas, as reported in the evening brief, will recommend Netanyahu.
Herzog's consultations open Wednesday, starting with smaller parties, with Likud last on Thursday evening; the nominee then gets 28 days, extendable by 14. Sources:
Source: themedialine.org.

item.title: Ukraine update: aid-centre toll rises to 31 as outages and water cuts spread
item.description:
The death toll from Monday's strike on the humanitarian aid centre and shelter in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, has risen to 31, with more than 45 people still missing, according to the New York Post's wire report. Rescuers were still searching the cratered site on Tuesday. The overnight barrage itself — 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles, as President Volodymyr Zelensky reported — is the same wave covered in this morning's brief; what changed during the day is the scale of the civilian fallout now being counted.
Ukraine's national energy company said Russia attacked its energy facilities more than 20 times, forcing emergency power outages in seven regions including Kyiv, and scheduled cuts elsewhere left some consumers without electricity for more than 12 hours — the first such outages this autumn, according to Ukrainska Pravda via the Post. Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia also hit a substation critical to the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant, calling it a threat to the nuclear safety of all of Europe and saying he had spoken to the International Atomic Energy Agency. Major water supply facilities left without power interrupted Kyiv's water supply. DTEK, Ukraine's largest private generator, called it one of the most serious attacks ever on its facilities, with three of its five thermal plants halted. The UN Secretary-General condemned the continuing attacks on population centres, including strikes on a medical facility and a hospice in Kharkiv and Dnipro, and noted the record civilian casualties.
Diplomatically, the day moved in two directions at once. Zelensky travelled to Germany for talks with European leaders ahead of next week's US-brokered talks, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed on Tuesday that a Russian delegation will attend the Abu Dhabi talks on November 10–11 — the first such talks since February. No ceasefire or de-escalation was announced by either side.
Sources:
Source: nypost.com.

item.title: Iran update: "no rush" from Trump, "far from a deal" from Tehran — while the Qeshm strike stays unconfirmed on the record
item.description:
No government has put the Qeshm Island strike on the record. As of Tuesday afternoon US time, multiple US officials had told CNN, AP, the BBC/CBS and others that the US carried out limited "defensive" strikes on Qeshm on Monday after Iranian surface-to-air fire against US aircraft or assets, targeting radar and missile launchers — the Wall Street Journal first reported the operation — but US Central Command had issued no formal public statement and Iranian authorities had not formally confirmed a US attack on the island, according to NewsCubby's Tuesday update and The Media Line. IRNA reported several explosions on Qeshm on Monday night.
The two sides' public lines pulled in opposite directions on Tuesday. Trump told Axios on Monday there is "no rush" to decide on new strikes — "one way or the other, we will do something" — and told NBC News he was not considering striking Iran after the midterms, while also again raising Pickaxe Mountain, the suspected underground nuclear site, as a target. A senior Iranian official told Reuters the two sides are far from a deal and that Tehran will not accept Washington's "excessive demands," and parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said Iran had given the US a "strong and rational response" and that "the ball is in the US' court." Qatari mediators were due in Tehran on Tuesday night to meet Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, according to Reuters via The Media Line. Oil, which fell sharply on Monday — Brent down 7.6% to $104.77, its biggest one-day drop since July — gave back part of that fall on Tuesday after the strike news broke.
Sources:
Source: newscubby.com.

item.title: Saudi–Houthi: reported cross-border ground raids, and the Asian Cup postponed
item.description:
A new report says the Houthi war has crossed a line beyond missiles and drones. Middle East Eye, citing a Western and an Arab official with direct knowledge, reports that Houthi fighters have launched multiple small-scale cross-border ground raids into Saudi Arabia's mountainous southwest in recent months, targeting border posts, with at least one raid as recently as the end of October — and that the raiders appear to have captured small arms and surveillance equipment used only by Saudi border forces. That account is relayed by OilPrice/ZeroHedge and has not been confirmed by Riyadh or the Houthis, so treat the scale as reported, not established. Separately, Bloomberg reports that the Asian Football Confederation has postponed its flagship tournament in Saudi Arabia until late 2027, citing "exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region" — the latest major event to slip as Houthi attacks continue. On the diplomatic side, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman discussed de-escalation efforts with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth by phone on Monday, and the coalition said it intercepted two drones targeting the Riyadh region on Monday night.
Sources:
Source: oilprice.com.

item.title: Israel update: Shas backs Netanyahu as Herzog's consultations open Wednesday
item.description:
The opposition's Eisenkot plan, covered in full this morning, gained a counterweight on Tuesday: the ultra-Orthodox Shas party said it will recommend Benjamin Netanyahu to President Isaac Herzog, citing his commitment to regulating the status of Torah students, according to Yedioth Ahronoth via The Insight International. Herzog begins consultations with parliamentary factions on Wednesday — starting with the smaller parties, with Likud last on Thursday evening — and the Central Elections Committee is expected to announce final official results on Wednesday. The new Knesset is sworn in on November 10. Nothing in Tuesday's announcements changes the arithmetic from this morning: Netanyahu's bloc 53, the Jewish opposition 48, the Arab-led parties 19, with 61 needed. KAN also reported on Monday that Eisenkot has ruled out serving in a Netanyahu-led government.
Sources:
Source: theinsightinternational.com.

item.title: Google — Guided Learning reaches Classroom, and school AI goes opt-in:
item.description:
Google announced on November 3 that Guided Learning — the Gemini mode that coaches students through a problem rather than handing them the answer — is now globally available in Google Classroom, with a pilot in Search at select US schools later in November.
The bigger policy change: Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until a school administrator explicitly turns them on. The catch, flagged by 9to5Google and the New York Times: because Search and AI are "deeply integrated," schools that keep AI off also lose Search for their students, with two options promised for early 2027 — AI features on, or Guided Learning in their place.
Sources:
Source: blog.google.

item.title: CISA KEV — WordPress core added Tuesday:
item.description:
CISA updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Tuesday afternoon for the first time since Friday, to version 2026.11.03 with 1,767 entries.
The one new entry is WordPress core CVE-2026-119977 — a flaw in the core update process where a staged copy of WordPress under wp-content/upgrade/ could be reached by an unauthenticated attacker during an upgrade window. Wordfence rates it 8.1; the fix is WordPress 7.1.4 or the matching backport.
Federal agencies have until Friday, November 6. Source:
Source: carthageelectronics.com.

item.title: Node-RED flaw CVE-2026-58115 exploited in the wild:
item.description:
A CVSS 10.0 missing-authentication bug in the Node-RED HTTP interface bundled with Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices (Industrial OS) — an unauthenticated attacker can deploy a flow and run commands with full privileges.
VulnCheck observed the first attack on October 30 and 16 attempts by November 1, dropping Linux bots and flow-based webshells. Fixed in Industrial OS V4.3.4.1.
Not yet on CISA's KEV list as of November 3. Source:
Source: threataft.com.

item.title: Binance follow-up — outflows slowing:
item.description:
Net outflows fell to $2.57 billion on Monday from $6.1 billion on Sunday, according to DefiLlama data cited by Cointelegraph, and Binance also reopened withdrawals for several fiat currencies including the US dollar.
The exchange warned of scammers impersonating it to offer accelerated withdrawals or "Binance vault" transfers. The next reserves snapshot is due Wednesday.
Caveat as before: the 95% replenishment figure is the company's own claim, not an independent audit. Source:
Source: cointelegraph.com.

item.title: Poland's top court splits in two — eight judges meet, seven stay away, and both sides claim the law
item.description:
Poland's Constitutional Tribunal held its disputed general assembly on Tuesday, and the result was two courts claiming to be one. Eight judges, all elected by the current Sejm, met in Warsaw under Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who suspended the tribunal's president and deputy on October 30. They ruled that they formed a quorum by counting 12 eligible judges — leaving out the suspended president Bogdan Święczkowski and deputy Bartłomiej Sochański, plus Judge Jarosław Wyrembak, whose election Korwin-Piotrowska called defective — and then adopted the tribunal's draft 2027 budget and drew lots for the disciplinary panels that will hear the cases of Święczkowski and Sochański. That is what RMF24 and Notes from Poland reported, via Crisis.Zone's live tracker. The other seven judges, including Święczkowski, stayed away; he dismissed the meeting as a "social gathering," and constitutional law expert Ryszard Piotrowski called it illegal.
The details behind the quorum fight matter because the whole crisis turns on a counting question. The tribunal has 15 seats, and a general assembly normally needs 10 judges present. Only eight judges elected by the current Sejm exist, so a 10-of-15 quorum was impossible without the other camp — which is why the eight redefined the denominator to 12. The budget vote was the practical trigger: without an approved revenue-and-expenditure plan, the tribunal's funds were not in next year's draft budget, and two earlier attempts to hold the assembly failed for lack of quorum, according to Interia's report of the meeting. Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek told Dziennik Gazeta Prawna that his immunity-lifting motions do not need a quorum, though adopting the budget does — and on Tuesday he filed a sixth motion to lift Święczkowski's immunity. Prosecutors separately opened an investigation into the alleged assault on judges Korwin-Piotrowska and Krystian Markiewicz at the building's entrance during President Karol Nawrocki's entry on October 31.
Each side's legal argument is now on the record, and neither has been tested before a body both accept. The government-backed judges say the Sejm's power to elect judges is constitutional, that the suspended leadership blocked the court from functioning, and that the European Commission and the Venice Commission back parliament's appointment power — the Commission said on Saturday that appointing the eight new members lies within the Sejm's constitutional power. The other camp, backed by the Supreme Court's College, says a suspension from duties does not end the president's term or create a vacancy, so Korwin-Piotrowska cannot lawfully direct the court; the College adopted a resolution on Tuesday saying the move to suspend the president and vice-president lacked a legal basis, with all 55 judges present backing it, according to PolandInsight. Nawrocki's camp calls the whole episode a forcible takeover — the tribunal's X account has used the word "coup" — while Prime Minister Donald Tusk has said restoring the rule of law is a duty and that there can be no compromise. The Supreme Court's own general assembly on Tuesday fell short of the quorum needed to adopt a resolution, leaving the College's statement as the judiciary's main counterweight.
For ordinary Poles, the immediate stakes are less abstract than the quorum maths. A paralysed constitutional court cannot rule on the laws parliament passes, the budget process for the court itself was the tripwire, and the standoff is already spilling into the street and the currency market: riot police were deployed at the court on Friday, protesters have gathered outside it for days, and Commerzbank noted on Tuesday that the institutional conflict is weighing on the zloty, with EUR/PLN briefly reaching 4.4372. With a general election a year away, both camps are also fighting over who gets to define the crisis — restoration of the rule of law, or a coup against a constitutional body.
In short: eight judges met, called themselves a quorum by counting 12 instead of 15, passed the 2027 budget and set disciplinary panels in motion against the suspended president and deputy — while the other seven judges stayed away, the Supreme Court's College said the suspensions had no legal basis, prosecutors opened an assault investigation, and the question of who lawfully runs Poland's top court remains unanswered by any body both sides accept.
Sources:
Source: crisis.zone.

item.title: Russell Brand — jury deliberations have begun:
item.description:
The jury in the trial of Russell Brand began deliberating on Tuesday at London's Southwark Crown Court, after Judge Joel Bennathan finished summing up and sent them out just before 14:50 GMT, Reuters reports.
Brand denies three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault, involving six women over 1999–2009. No verdict yet, and nothing here is a finding of guilt.
Source:
Source: wnflsports.com.

item.title: Russia's election-day barrage hits Ukraine's power grid as the aid-centre toll rises to 29
item.description:
Russia launched a sweeping overnight bombardment of Ukraine's energy infrastructure on Tuesday, hours after the death toll from Monday's strike on a humanitarian aid centre in Zaporizhzhia rose to 29, with 48 people still missing. The barrage — 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky — triggered emergency power cuts across the country and landed on the day of the US midterm elections, a timing Zelensky pointedly flagged.
The details, as reported by the Associated Press and Reuters, show a two-front night. In Komyshuvakha, the Zaporizhzhia village hit Monday, rescuers kept pulling bodies from the cratered aid facility and shelter through Tuesday, with acting regional military chief Mykhailo Semikin calling it "one of the worst tragedies in terms of the number of civilian victims in our region since the start of the full-scale war." The region declared three days of mourning. In the overnight wave, a strike on a city clinical hospital in Kharkiv wounded at least 62 people by local authorities' count — Zelensky put the hospital toll at 73 — and forced the transfer of more than 200 patients; in Dnipro, one person was killed and 17 wounded, with a woman pulled alive from rubble Tuesday morning. Ukraine's largest private generator, DTEK, said three of its five thermal power plants were knocked offline, and railways were hit as well. Russia's Defence Ministry said it carried out a "massive strike" on electricity facilities supplying military factories and on port infrastructure in Odesa. In the other direction, Ukraine's drones set fire to a major oil refinery in Yaroslavl, wounding two employees, according to the regional governor; Moscow's mayor said 493 drones were fired toward the capital, and Moscow-installed officials in Crimea imposed rolling blackouts after energy attacks there.
The two sides read the night in opposite ways. Zelensky framed the timing as a message to Washington: "The Russians think America won't notice this signal of theirs," he said, urging the US to "help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes." Moscow's account is purely military: its Defence Ministry described strikes on facilities supplying Ukraine's army and arms factories, with no comment on the Komyshuvakha aid centre or the Kharkiv hospital. The gap between those accounts is the story — one side presenting a deliberate signal to an election-day America, the other presenting routine strikes on war infrastructure.
For ordinary people, the impact is heat, light and hospital beds. Emergency and unscheduled outages spread from Odesa in the south to Rivne in the west, three DTEK plants are offline, and hospital patients in two cities were moved mid-treatment. The Komyshuvakha search continues under the threat of further strikes, with dozens of families still waiting to learn whether the missing are alive. The diplomatic calendar adds pressure: US envoy Steve Witkoff has said Washington will mediate working-level talks between Ukrainian and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11, a week after a night like this one.
In short: at least 29 dead and 48 missing from Monday's aid-centre strike, a 365-weapon overnight barrage that knocked out power plants and hit hospitals, Kyiv reading it as an election-day signal to Washington, Moscow calling it strikes on military supply — and Abu Dhabi talks a week away.
Sources:
Source: npr.brightspotcdn.com.

item.title: US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island land on the eve of the midterms — while Doha mediators report progress
item.description:
The United States carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, the Wall Street Journal first reported, citing US officials — and three US officials confirmed the operation to CNN, describing it as defensive. The strike, on an island at the western end of the Strait of Hormuz that hosts IRGC naval and missile bases, came the same day Qatari mediators reported progress in indirect US–Iran talks, and on the eve of the US midterm elections after which President Donald Trump has been expected to decide on wider strikes.
The details, as reported by CNN, USA Today and the Journal via multiple relays, are still thin on damage. One US official said the strike came in response to Iran firing at a US aircraft; another described it as "a defensive measure for Iranians using surface-to-air missiles against US assets." The Journal reported that the US has carried out other such limited strikes in recent weeks without announcing them, to avoid signalling a return to major combat. Iran's state-affiliated Fars agency reported several explosions heard on Qeshm in the early hours of Tuesday local time, also heard on nearby Hengam Island and in Bandar Abbas. The IRGC claimed it shot down two US reconnaissance drones over Qeshm and destroyed an MQ-9 east of the strait — claims US Central Command has disputed in part and that remain unverified. Neither government has confirmed a strike on the record, and no targets, damage or casualties have been independently established.
Each side's public posture points in a different direction. Washington's line, through unnamed officials, is that this was protective, not escalatory — and one person familiar with the matter told CNN the administration deliberately kept it under wraps "in an effort not to overstate the defensive move." Tehran's deputy foreign minister, Kazem Gharibabadi, downplayed the incident as part of an "ongoing war" while reserving the right to defend itself, and parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned early Tuesday that any enemy miscalculation would meet an "unpredictable" military and strategic response. At the same time, the diplomacy track moved: Qatar's foreign ministry said its mediation team had returned to Doha after talks in Tehran, that "clear progress is emerging," and that both sides are reviewing the mediators' proposals; CNN cited diplomats saying responses are expected within two days. Vice President JD Vance said Monday the two sides have "made some progress" toward an off-ramp. Trump, for his part, told Fox News the war is "a very soft war," said a deal "could happen," and again raised Pickaxe Mountain, the suspected underground nuclear site, as a target he could hit "in one hour" whenever he wants.
For ordinary people, the stakes run through fuel prices. Oil rose in early Asian trading Tuesday after the strike news broke, after falling Monday on hopes for a deal — and CNN notes gasoline and diesel prices are on track to be the most expensive of any US Election Day in history. The strait, through which about 20 million barrels of oil a day passed before the war, is the reason a limited strike on one island moves pump prices on another continent. The two-day Hormuz reopening offer Tehran has floated — blockade lifted, sanctions waived, frozen assets released, then the strait reopens — remains the shape of any deal, and Washington's answer is still outstanding.
In short: a limited, unannounced US strike on Qeshm that Washington calls defensive and Tehran calls part of an ongoing war, landing hours before Americans vote, while Qatari mediators say the talks are making real progress and expect answers within two days. The strike and the talks are now racing each other.
Sources:
Source: cnn.com.

Trump, for his part, told Fox News the war is "a very soft war," said a deal "could happen," and again raised Pickaxe Mountain, the suspected underground nuclear site, as a target he could hit "in one hour" whenever he wants.

For ordinary people, the stakes run through fuel prices. Oil rose in early Asian trading Tuesday after the strike news broke, after falling Monday on hopes for a deal — and CNN notes gasoline and diesel prices are on track to be the most expensive of any US Election Day in history. The strait, through which about 20 million barrels of oil a day passed before the war, is the reason a limited strike on one island moves pump prices on another continent. The two-day Hormuz reopening offer Tehran has floated — blockade lifted, sanctions waived, frozen assets released, then the strait reopens — remains the shape of any deal, and Washington's answer is still outstanding.

In short: a limited, unannounced US strike on Qeshm that Washington calls defensive and Tehran calls part of an ongoing war, landing hours before Americans vote, while Qatari mediators say the talks are making real progress and expect answers within two days. The strike and the talks are now racing each other.

item.title: Israel's opposition agrees on Eisenkot — but the coalition maths still doesn't work
item.description:
Israel's opposition leaders held their first joint meeting since the October 27 election on Tuesday morning in Herzliya, and came out with a single candidate and a plan: all participating parties will recommend Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot to President Isaac Herzog for the first mandate to form a government, their negotiating teams will immediately begin drafting guiding principles and coalition agreements, and they will move to replace the Knesset speaker at the first opportunity.
The details, as reported by Israel RealTime and Anadolu via DailyImroz, show agreement on the candidate but not on the coalition. The joint statement, issued under the Change and Reform parties, pledged a "National Emergency Government" and a "Zionist government" built on Eisenkot's four principles, and accused Likud and Netanyahu of a campaign to delegitimise the election results. Former prime minister Naftali Bennett said his Beyachad party "will fully mobilize to help Gadi Eisenkot form a government as soon as possible." But the arithmetic is unchanged: Netanyahu's bloc holds 53 of 120 seats, the Jewish opposition 48, the Arab-led parties 19, and 61 are needed. Yair Golan's position in favour of a government with the Arab parties remained a minority view at the meeting, Avigdor Liberman still refuses a government that includes or depends on Arab parties, and Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen told CNN he will not join a coalition because he "cannot take responsibility for military actions against our Palestinian people." A separate wrinkle: Liberman said his party will back Yair Lapid for Knesset speaker, a move Channel 12 analyst Amit Segal read as pushing toward another election — while figures in Eisenkot's own party said Lapid will not become speaker, arguing it would kill almost all chances of forming a government.
Each side's argument is about legitimacy versus arithmetic. The opposition says it has a parliamentary majority for change and a decisive public vote, and that replacing the speaker and taking the mandate are the first steps to acting on it. Netanyahu's camp says he must lead any broad government and rejects one dependent on the Arab parties; his bloc, with 53 seats, remains the largest. Herzog begins two days of consultations with factions on Wednesday, starting with the smaller parties, and whoever he taps gets 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension.
For ordinary Israelis, the practical consequence is a caretaker government that stays in place while the deadlock plays out: Netanyahu remains prime minister until a new government is sworn in, and the two routes to 61 — a minority arrangement Liberman has ruled out, or a unity government Eisenkot has ruled out joining under Netanyahu — are both blocked by the people who would have to agree to them. Eisenkot is also due to begin receiving direct Shin Bet protection on Wednesday.
In short: the opposition now speaks with one voice behind Eisenkot and has a plan for the Knesset's first days, but 48 plus Arab recommendations it won't govern on still isn't a coalition — and Wednesday's presidential consultations are where that contradiction gets tested.
Sources:
Source: israelrealtime.com.

item.title: Poland's tribunal assembly convenes today — outcome pending:
item.description:
Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska's general assembly of Constitutional Tribunal judges is scheduled for 3:30 PM Warsaw time (8:30 AM CT), with the quorum dispute unresolved — she says 10 of the fixed 15 judges are needed; PiS figures have advised judges not to attend and dispute it is an assembly at all.
New since the night brief: the International Commission of Jurists called on all Polish institutions to resolve the crisis through the rule of law and warned against using police or criminal proceedings to change the court's composition; President Nawrocki convened the National Security Council for Tuesday over the tribunal situation, and the Supreme Court president called an extraordinary general assembly of Supreme Court judges the same day. The Prosecutor General has also filed five motions to lift the immunities of tribunal president Święczkowski and his deputy.
Sources:
Source: pollar.news.

item.title: Saudi–Houthi claims, Tuesday:
item.description:
The Houthis announced strikes on Jizan airport and other Saudi sites Tuesday morning — unconfirmed by Saudi authorities, and carried here only as a Houthi claim.
Coalition interception reports also circulated overnight via thin aggregator relays; no casualty or damage figure is verified. The US Embassy's November 2 security alert (non-emergency staff ordered out since October 23, special authorisation for airport use, Riyadh airport partially reopened) was already covered in the night brief.
Source:
Source: indianeconomicobserver.com.

item.title: Apple — iOS 27.3 beta lands November 3:
item.description:
Apple began seeding the iOS 27.3 beta to developers in the US on November 3, with a China build set for November 4 and a public rollout expected in early to mid-December, according to BigGo Finance's roundup.
The headline item is the first broad deployment of Apple Intelligence on Chinese iPhones (Alibaba's Qwen powering writing tools, visual intelligence and AirPods live translation; iPhone 15 and newer only), plus a redesigned Health app that had slipped from the iOS 27.2 beta. This follows the October 31 announcement of the China rollout — the beta is the next step, not a new announcement.
Source:
Source: finance.biggo.com.
